entries.content: Project is a VS Code extension with embedded LSP server — two webpack entry points: src/extension.ts (client) and src/server/server.ts (server)
Server code organized into subsystems: core/, lsp/, ck3/, schema/, data/, log/, utils/ — uses functional composition over inheritance and coordinator pattern for validation
kanban-development-guideline.md is the single-source-of-truth for all coding standards, workflow, and forbidden practices — always consult it before making changes
Prettier: printWidth 100, tabWidth 4 (spaces only), semicolons required, single quotes, trailing commas es5, bracket spacing, arrow parens always
Naming: camelCase for variables/functions, PascalCase for interfaces/types/classes, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants, kebab-case.ts for file names
Never use 'any' type — use 'unknown' with type guards. Never use 'var' — only const/let. Never use loose equality (==) — use strict (===)
No console.log in production code — use the project's logger. No throw literals — always throw Error objects
Use Taskfile wrapper commands (task build, task test, task lint, task format) at workspace root, or npm scripts in vscode-extension/
Pre-commit hooks run 8 checks including formatting, linting, YAML/JSON validation — never skip them with --no-verify
Branching model: main (stable), develop (integration), feature/* (features). No new dependencies without explicit permission
Formic task system: tasks live in .formic/tasks/t-{name}/, board state in .formic/board.json, subtasks in subtasks.json, declared files in declared-files.json

The architect decomposition pattern works well for large migration tasks — decompose into independent cleanup subtasks (config, tests, docs, scripts, AI configs, comments) plus a final verification gate that depends on all others

TypeScript migration is functionally complete (commit d13348d): all 53 features reimplemented, 225 unit tests added, 17 audit issues fixed. Remaining work is purely artifact cleanup across 7 child tasks (t-2 through t-8)
When removing legacy Python config (pythonPath), do NOT remove the 'args' setting in package.json — it is legitimate and used in extension.ts:1046

CK3 game data uses 'legacy' terminology (e.g. dynasty_legacy, legacy format) — these are game concepts, NOT references to the Python migration. Never remove comments containing 'legacy' in completions.ts, loader.ts, or validator.ts without verifying context
Project name 'pychivalry' is the brand name, not a Python reference — preserve it throughout documentation even after full TypeScript migration
Child tasks t-2 through t-7 are independent and can be parallelized; t-8 (verification) depends on all six. Current status: t-2 is in briefing, t-3 through t-7 are queued, t-8 is blocked

The .vscode/settings.json has interleaved Python and TypeScript settings — when cleaning, preserve all ck3LanguageServer.* settings (enable, logLevel, trace, logWatcher), editor settings, and Node.js exclusions (node_modules, dist)

tools/ directory has 3 scripts needing Python removal: setup-dev-env.sh (bash), Check-Prerequisites.ps1 (PowerShell), Install-Prerequisites.ps1 (PowerShell). All should reference Node.js 18+, npm, task commands only

Migration commit messages should enumerate specific changes: features added count, tests added count, issues fixed count, with categorized bullet points (Critical/Stubs/Dead code/Missing diagnostics/Consistency)

For verifying migration completeness, search for these terms and expect zero hits (excluding node_modules, dist, Documentation/): pythonPath, pygls, pip install, pytest, setup.py, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt
When removing an obsolete config setting, check three layers: package.json contributes.configuration (declaration), runtime code that reads it, and test assertions. All three must be cleaned.
configuration.test.ts stores originalConfig for restore-after-test; when removing a setting, also remove it from that backup object, not just from test cases.
pythonPath was a leftover from the original Python-based server. The extension is now pure TypeScript with an embedded LSP server—no Python dependency remains.
Use grep -r across vscode-extension/ with --include='*.ts' --include='*.json' to confirm zero remaining references after removing an obsolete symbol.

When removing legacy Python settings from .vscode/settings.json, clean up all related categories: interpreter path, linting, formatting, testing, file excludes (__pycache__, *.pyc, .pytest_cache), search excludes, and python-envs settings
The ck3LanguageServer.pythonPath setting was also a legacy Python artifact that needed removal alongside the python.* settings
Legacy settings can be scattered across multiple sections of settings.json (top-level, files.exclude, search.exclude) — must audit all sections, not just the obvious python.* namespace
Project has migrated from Python to TypeScript. Tasks t-1 through t-8 track the full migration cleanup. Task board is in .formic/board.json

Development setup scripts (tools/setup-dev-env.sh, tools/Check-Prerequisites.ps1, tools/Install-Prerequisites.ps1) now target a TypeScript-only workflow: Node.js 18+, npm ci in vscode-extension/, task build/test:unit/lint commands, F5 debug launch. All Python/pip/pytest references removed.

Install-Prerequisites.ps1 uses a data-driven $Prerequisites array of hashtables (Name, WingetId, MinVersion, Commands, VersionPattern) making it easy to add/remove tools. Current entries: Git, Node.js, VS Code, GitHub CLI.

setup-dev-env.sh uses semantic version parsing for Node.js checks: extract version with sed 's/^v//', get major with cut -d'.' -f1, then numeric comparison. Pre-commit install is conditional (command -v pre-commit) with || true on pre-commit run.

When rewriting scripts to remove a technology (e.g. Python), must also remove related helper functions (Test-PythonPackage, Test-PipPackage) and parameters (SkipPythonPackages) that become dead code, not just the sections that call them.
Project has been renamed from 'PyChivalry'/'pychivalry' to 'ck3-language-support' in user-facing messaging. Update references in any new scripts or docs.

All three setup scripts use consistent next-steps messaging: npm ci in vscode-extension/, task build, task test:unit, task lint, and F5 launch in VS Code. Keep these in sync when updating any one script.

Documentation migration task t-5 updated 4 files (README.md, vscode-extension/README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, vscode-extension/CHANGELOG.md) — removed all Python references (pip, pytest, pygls, pythonPath, Black, flake8, mypy, Python 3.9+) and replaced with TypeScript/Node.js equivalents (npm, Node.js 18+, vscode-languageserver, task commands)
When updating user-facing docs after a language migration, verify with grep for banned terms across all target files as a final validation step — ensures no stale references survive
The project name 'pychivalry' is intentionally kept despite the Python-to-TypeScript migration — it is the project brand and must never be renamed

The extension uses an embedded LSP server (no separate installation required) — user docs must state that VS Code is the only prerequisite beyond Node.js 18+; no pip install or pythonPath configuration
Root README badge was changed from Python 3.9+ to Node.js 18+; acknowledgments section replaced pygls with vscode-languageserver ^9.0.1

CHANGELOG.md contained forward-looking Python instructions (pythonPath setting in v0.1.0 config table, Python Detection features in v0.2.0) that looked like historical records but were actually never-shipped Python features — these needed removal, not just annotation
Formic task t-5 had 19 subtasks across 4 files — granular subtask decomposition (one per logical section per file) made the documentation sweep systematic and prevented missed references

When cleaning migration-era comments, distinguish between comments referencing the migration itself (remove/rewrite) and comments using 'legacy' to describe domain concepts like CK3 game-data formats (preserve unchanged)
For comment-only changes, always run `task lint` and `task format:check` afterward — whitespace and formatting regressions can slip in when rewriting multi-line comment blocks

Replace comparative/historical comments ('doesn't have X like Y') with positive, self-contained descriptions of current behavior ('Single-threaded event-loop model — all requests handled sequentially')
The .gitignore had stale section headers ('# Reference repositories') that became empty after removing entries — always check for orphaned section comments when deleting .gitignore lines
After removing references to a keyword (e.g. 'Python', 'pygls'), grep the entire TypeScript source tree to confirm no remaining occurrences before declaring the task complete
